extra.message: User-controlled request body fields (req.body.preTax, req.body.afterTax, req.body.roth) are passed directly to eval(). An attacker can submit a value such as 'process.exit()' or arbitrary JavaScript, resulting in server-side JavaScript (code) injection and remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')

extra.message: The user-supplied 'threshold' query parameter is interpolated directly into a MongoDB $where JavaScript expression (this.stocks > '${threshold}'). This allows NoSQL/JavaScript injection, e.g. threshold = "0' || true || '" or "';while(true){}" leading to data disclosure or denial of service.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: The allocations userId is taken from the URL route parameter (req.params.userId) instead of the authenticated session (req.session.userId). Any logged-in user can request /allocations/<other-user-id> and view another user's asset allocation data (IDOR / broken access control).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The /benefits GET and POST routes only require isLoggedIn and omit the isAdmin middleware. The admin-only functionality (viewing and updating all users' benefits) is therefore accessible to any authenticated non-admin user, and updateBenefits accepts an arbitrary userId from the request body.

cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: The request query parameters 'url' and 'symbol' are concatenated and passed to needle.get() without validation. An authenticated attacker can set url to an internal address (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ or http://localhost:27017) causing the server to perform arbitrary requests (SSRF), and the response body is written back to the client as text/html.

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

extra.message: The /learn route redirects to an unvalidated, user-supplied URL from req.query.url. An attacker can craft /learn?url=https://evil.example to redirect users to a malicious site (open redirect / unvalidated redirect).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: Swig's autoescape is explicitly disabled (autoescape: false). All template variables (user profile fields, memo content, login username, etc.) are rendered without HTML encoding, enabling reflected and stored cross-site scripting throughout the application.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The userName value supplied in the login POST body is re-rendered into the value attribute with autoescape disabled (session.js handleLoginRequest passes userName back on failure). Payloads such as "><script>alert(1)</script> result in reflected XSS.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: firstNameSafeString (the raw firstName supplied in the profile update request) is placed into an href attribute with autoescape disabled. Because it is HTML-encoded only in some contexts, an attacker can inject a javascript: URL or break out of the attribute to execute script (XSS in URL context).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: Passwords are stored in the users collection in cleartext (the password value is written directly, and validateLogin compares them with a plain '==='). A database compromise exposes all user credentials; bcrypt hashing is commented out.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: After a successful login the session is not regenerated; req.session.userId is set on the existing session. An attacker who fixes/knows a victim's pre-authentication session id can reuse it after login (session fixation).

cwe: CWE-384: Session Fixation

extra.message: The error handler logs and renders the full error object (including message and stack trace) into error-template.html, disclosing internal implementation details, file paths, and database errors to the client.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Highly sensitive PII (SSN and date of birth) is stored in cleartext in the users collection and returned to the client. The encryption code that would protect these fields is commented out, so a database or response leak exposes sensitive data.

cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information

extra.message: The express-session cookie is configured without the HttpOnly (and Secure) flags; the HttpOnly setting is commented out. Client-side scripts can read the session cookie, amplifying XSS impact and allowing session theft over unencrypted HTTP.

cwe: CWE-1004: Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag

extra.message: CSRF protection is disabled: the csurf middleware require and app.use(csrf()) are commented out, so state-changing POST endpoints (profile, contributions, benefits, memos) can be triggered cross-site without a token.

cwe: CWE-352: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)

extra.message: The regex /([0-9]+)+\#/ applied to the user-controlled bankRouting field is vulnerable to catastrophic backtracking (ReDoS). A crafted input of many digits causes exponential CPU consumption and can hang the server.

cwe: CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption

extra.message: The attacker-controlled userName from the login request is written directly into the application log. CRLF characters in the value can forge additional log entries (log injection / log forging).

cwe: CWE-117: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs

extra.message: The signup password policy /^.{1,20}$/ accepts any 1-character password, allowing extremely weak credentials. The stronger policy requiring length, digits, and mixed case is commented out.

cwe: CWE-521: Weak Password Requirements

extra.message: The session cookie signing secret is hardcoded in source control ('session_cookie_secret_key_here'), and a hardcoded ZAP API key appears in config/env/development.js. Anyone with repository access can forge signed session cookies.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: The application is served exclusively over plain HTTP (http.createServer); the HTTPS server code is commented out. Session cookies and credentials are transmitted in cleartext, exposing them to interception.

cwe: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
